I've spent ten years building data analytics infrastructure for
growth-stage companies — the past eight moving one from guessing to
measuring. I founded and lead its analytics and data science department,
and have taken new business verticals through the full data maturity
model: collection, reporting, prediction, automated optimization. My
domain is marketplace and auction mechanics in consumer lending —
real-time bidding, lead routing, fraud, experimentation — and my daily
work is translating data science into decisions that hold up in front of
both executives and engineers.

I hold an M.S. in Systems Science, where I studied applied and
theoretical modeling of systems. This site presents one project in
depth: **Tributary**, an end-to-end build that simulates a fractured
marketplace data environment, unifies it with measured accuracy, and
mines the unified view for decisions — directed by me, built with AI
agents, with the direction itself kept as an auditable record.

## Three proof points

**Provable unification.** Three architecturally real cloud silos (S3 Parquet
lake, transactional Postgres, BigQuery) are resolved to a single consumer
identity — and scored against a hidden ground-truth crosswalk the pipeline
never sees. Entity-resolution F1 of 0.87–0.88, with 95.3% of auction revenue
events made consumer-joinable, up from 0%.
[The silo problem →](tributary/silo-problem.qmd)

**Cost engineering as a discipline.** The entire three-silo cloud footprint
was deployed for one cent, held under a $10/month budget with alerting, and
instrumented with before/after receipts — including a 10.9x reduction in
warehouse bytes scanned from partitioning alone.
[Cost engineering →](tributary/cost.qmd)

**A working method you can audit.** Every phase ships with decision records,
an intervention log of agent errors and the corrections that fixed them, and
per-commit provenance decomposing human direction from agent execution.
[How this was built →](tributary/method.qmd)
